beats.say: A Dutch officer captured here then led his captors' army.
beats.cap: Captured at Colachel in 1741, he later led Travancore's army

beats.say: In seventeen forty-one, the Dutch East India Company occupied Colachel, in the kingdom of Travancore.
beats.cap: 1741: the Dutch East India Company (VOC) occupies Colachel

beats.say: Dutch letters say their whole Malabar field force was three hundred and fifty Europeans, plus Malays.
beats.cap: Dutch letters: whole Malabar field force 350 Europeans, 490 Malays
1741: Travancore's forces attack the Dutch post

beats.say: Dutch letters say a red-hot ball fired their gunpowder. The garrison surrendered.
beats.cap: Dutch letters: a red-hot ball fired the gunpowder · garrison surrendered

beats.say: Travancore's histories call it a battle won.
beats.cap: Travancore's histories: a battle won, Dutch prisoners taken

beats.say: Prisoner Eustachius De Lannoy then led Travancore's army, his tomb says for about thirty-seven years.
beats.cap: Eustachius De Lannoy · tomb: about 37 years in the king's service

beats.say: The peace treaty came years later. And the captive led his captors' army.
beats.cap: Peace treaty: years later · the captive led Travancore's army
